Apple basic version iPhone 18 will not launch until early 2027, but it may come with two new Pro series upgrades.

Analyst Jeff Pu says iPhone 18 will feature 12GB RAM and a new Dynamic Island design

Apple's annual September keynote is coming up, with iPhone 18 Pro and other new products expected to debut.

Reports suggest the basic iPhone 18 will not appear at the event. Apple will only unveil the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra.

However, the basic iPhone 18 will still arrive, just not until early 2027. It is expected to launch alongside the iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2.

According to analyst Jeff Pu, the iPhone 18 may include several Pro-series upgrades.

In the latest research note obtained by 9to5Mac, Pu laid out his expectations for the basic iPhone 18 based on his sources and supply chain checks. Two features stand out:

  • 12GB RAM, an upgrade over the 8GB in the iPhone 17
  • A new Dynamic Island design, which will debut on the iPhone 18 Pro

We have had conflicting reports about the iPhone 18's RAM before. Most recently, Ming-Chi Kuo said the device would only get 9GB RAM instead of 12GB.

Pu's note, however, says the iPhone 18e will have 9GB, while the iPhone 18 will get 12GB, even though both models will use the A20 chip.

The smaller Dynamic Island expected next month would also be a welcome upgrade.

When the Dynamic Island debuted on the iPhone 14 Pro, the basic iPhone 14 still used a notch. Apple did not bring the Dynamic Island to its lower-tier models until the iPhone 15.

But based on Pu's research, Apple may be looking to speed up the rollout of the new, smaller Dynamic Island design to the basic iPhone.

Are you interested in the basic iPhone 18, or planning to go Pro or Ultra? Let us know in the comments.
